messages:
Liam P.: hey all, Liam here, starting today. Ran `kubectl config get-contexts` and only see `minikube`. Need read access to `staging` and an onboarding ns `liam-onboard` with edit. Who should I ping and what do you need? :wave:

Nora (DevEx): welcome! :tada: Open an infra ticket and paste your flattened kubeconfig (`kubectl config view --minify --flatten`). Include corp email, manager, and exact perms (read/write). If on corp laptop you can run the cred helper: `curl -s https://go.redwood/get-kubecreds.sh | bash` (corp only).

Liam P.: pasted flattened kubeconfig:
```
apiVersion: v1
clusters: []
contexts: []
current-context: minikube
kind: Config
preferences: {}
users:
- name: minikube
```

I opened INF-2001 and cc'd @sylvia_m.

onboard-bot: ticket INF-2001 created and routed to eng-infra. https://tickets.redwood/INF-2001

Sam (Eng-Infra): hey Liam — process: we'll create `liam-onboard` and bind `edit`, add you to `redwood-staging-read`. If you need staging exec/create request temporary elevation with expiry. I'll apply bindings now and post when done.

Sam (Eng-Infra): done — rolebindings applied. Run to verify:
```
kubectl config get-contexts
kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=liam-onboard
kubectl auth can-i create deployments --namespace=staging
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=liam-onboard
```

Liam P.: verified: contexts now include `redwood-staging` and `liam-onboard`, `auth can-i` yes for list in my ns and no for create in staging (that's fine). I can deploy a test pod. Thanks! :raised_hands:

Nora (DevEx): pro tip: if you see duplicate contexts later run `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config && chmod 600 ~/.kube/config`. Also use `kubectl config use-context redwood-staging` to switch explicitly.
